rows.title: New client onboarding: the first 5 days (welcome pack, access list, audit, 30-day plan, kickoff)
rows.caption:
New client just signed? Here's what to do in the first 5 days (save this).

Day 0: send a welcome pack within 24 hours: how you work, where to reach you + your reply hours, payment terms, and what you need from them.
Day 1: ask for access (team or partner access, never passwords): Instagram, Meta business, scheduler, brand kit, last 90 days of posts, one shared folder.
Day 1–2: audit their last 90 days. What worked, what flopped, why.
Day 3–4: draft a 30-day plan.
Day 5: kickoff call. Show the audit + plan and agree on 4 things: what a win looks like in 90 days, who approves posts, when you're both online, and the first due date.

A calm first week is how a client decides you're worth keeping.

Send this to a freelancer who just signed a client 🤝

rows.title: 15-minute weekly reset: best post, plan 3 not 7, pick one thing to stop
rows.caption:
3 moves for a calmer week. Number 3 is the one people skip.

A 15-minute Sunday reset:
1. Find last week's best post. Ask why it worked: the hook, the topic, or the timing?
2. Plan 3 posts, not 7. Write just the hooks tonight. Three hooks you like beat seven you rushed.
3. Pick one thing to stop. One task that ate time and moved nothing (editing captions five times, checking views every hour).

Send this to the friend who plans seven and posts one.

rows.title: Score your caption's first line with Claude, then rewrite + add a specific (Byte fixes EP 4)
rows.caption:
Comment IDEA and I'll DM you the free Reel Idea Machine (a Claude skill + PDF guide).

Good reel, flat caption? Your first line is a hook too, and it decides if anyone taps "more".

1. Score it: paste your caption into Claude. "Score my caption's first line from 1 to 10. Would a stranger tap 'more'? Say why."
2. Rewrite it: ask for five rewrites that each name a problem.
3. Make it specific: add a number, a time, or a who.

Before: "Some thoughts on editing"
After: "3 edits that stop the swipe at second 2"

Score the first line before you post. Every time.
